name: Octaves
description: Adds the notes you play one and two octaves down and up, following chords note by note with no audible delay; dense chords come out a little rougher than single notes.

params.name: Two down
params.description: The level of the voice two octaves below what you play, with the weight of organ pedals. The lowest bass notes are left out, as two octaves under them is below hearing.

params.name: One down
params.description: The level of the voice one octave below what you play. It follows chords note for note, like a bass doubling every string. The very lowest notes are left out.

params.name: Dry
params.description: The level of your own sound, passed through untouched and in stereo. Turn it down to hear only the octaves.

params.name: One up
params.description: The level of the voice one octave above what you play. It adds the shimmer of a second, higher set of strings.

params.name: Two up
params.description: The level of the voice two octaves above what you play. Thin and bright, like the top stop of an organ.

params.name: Attack
params.description: How long the octaves take to fade in after each new note. At zero they start with the note; longer lets the pick or hammer through alone, then the octaves swell in.

params.name: Filter
params.description: A low-pass on the octave voices only. Turn it down to round off the upper octaves or to leave the low ones as a soft bass.

params.name: Resonance
params.description: A peak at the filter frequency, on the octave voices only. A little gives them a vocal, nasal edge; a lot makes the filter ring.

params.name: Detune
params.description: Pulls each octave voice slightly out of tune, each its own way. It makes the slow beating of a twelve-string or of a rank of organ pipes that are not quite in tune.

params.name: Spread
params.description: Places the notes of the two upper voices at different points between left and right. The lower octaves stay in the middle, and the sound sums to mono without loss.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit. A filter-bank octave generator after the approach of Etienne Thuillier, 'Real-Time Polyphonic Octave Doubling for the Guitar': the input is split into narrow complex band-pass channels, and each is played back with its phase doubled or halved and its level kept. The channel shape and layout, the phase equaliser, the channels that open wide for a moment at each new note, the turning down of channels in which two notes collide, and the sub-octave sign tracking are this device's own.
